title: lct translation batch
description: work/batches/<id>.json, written by `lct batch next`: the units to translate and everything a translator needs. The translation goes to work/batches/<id>.out.json (see batch-out.schema.json).

id.description: Batch id: the UTC time (yyyymmddThhmmss) and the first 8 hex digits of the sha256 of the first unit's key, with -2, -3... appended when that id was already in use.

family.description: File family of the batch's files (guides/routing.yaml); all of them are of it.

glossary_check.description: Present, as "warn", only when the family's glossary is a default and not a rule (guides/routing.yaml, glossary: warn): a glossary rendering missing from a translation is only a warning, and the translator may depart from it where the context does not fit, giving the reason in the note. Absent: a missing rendering is rejected unless the note names the term.

file.description: The first of files, such as StoryData/S1037B.json.

files.description: The pack files the units belong to, in the order they were handed out. A story batch has one; another batch may hold several files of its family. Each unit names its own in file.

guides.description: Guide files to read, relative to the repo root, in the order they layer (later ones refine earlier ones): those of the family, the files and the speakers of the units.

glossary.description: The approved glossary terms the units contain, each in the file of its unit. They bind.

jp.description: The word in the Japanese pack: one form, or a list of the forms it takes there. A unit whose jp holds any of them has the same word.

en.description: The word in the English pack: one form, or a list of the forms it takes there (Resistance, Resist). A unit whose en holds any of them has the same word.

forbidden.description: Renderings the translation must not contain; an entry starting with "re:" is a regular expression.

also.description: Other correct renderings of the term, beside zh. Choose between zh and these by notes; a translation that uses one of them needs no note.

match.description: Absent or "word": the term applies where its KR stands as a word (a following particle or ending such as 로, 가 or 니까 still counts), not inside a longer word. "substring": it applies wherever its KR occurs, inside a longer word too.

check.description: Absent or "warn": the rendering zh is the project's default, and a translation without it is accepted with a warning. "hard": a translation without zh is sent back unless the note names the KR term and the reason (a batch with glossary_check: warn only warns). "off": general vocabulary; zh is offered as a rendering, and a translation without it draws no warning. A forbidden rendering is always sent back.

meaning.description: The sense the entry stands for, in a few words. Weigh it, with this entry's jp and en, against the unit's own jp and en: if the KR in the unit means something else, do not use zh and say so in the note.

sources.description: Where meaning comes from: game:<file>#<pointer> (a key of the game files) or a https://limbuscompany.wiki.gg/ URL.

provisional.description: true: a provisional term registered earlier in this project and awaiting confirmation. Use it like any other entry.

files.description: The file patterns the term is written for; an item may also be family:<id>, which stands for the units of a batch whose family is <id>, or group:<node>, chapter:<n>, character:<id> or event:<name>, which go by the file's node and tag. Absent, it is for every file. A term with files applies only to the units whose file matches one of them, and for those units it takes the place of a term of the same kr without files.

not_files.description: The file patterns the term does not apply to, written like files (family:<id> included: the units of a batch whose family is <id>; also group:<node>, chapter:<n>, character:<id> and event:<name>). A unit whose file matches one of them is not held to this term, and gets no rendering from it.

units.description: The keys of the units of this batch that use the term. The scope (files, not_files) and the longer-entry rule are already counted in: a unit not listed here need not use the term, even if its KR holds the word.

keywords.description: Keyword [ID]s of the units (without brackets) and the name this translation gives them. Keep the [ID] itself in the text; the name is for understanding.

names.description: Existing renderings of the names the units use (skills, personas, E.G.O, effects: the name fields), capped by batch.max_names in lct.yaml. Not rules: use zh where the unit means the same thing (match the unit's jp, en and field against the item's), or follow the context and say so in the unit's note. One item for each (kr, variant); several items of one kr are the ways the JP and EN packs spell it.

zh.description: The rendering most units of this variant use.

count.description: The number of units that have zh.

others.description: The other renderings of this variant and the units that have each.

jp.description: The name in the Japanese pack, in those units.

en.description: The name in the English pack, in those units.

units.description: The keys of the units of this batch the name is for, in batch order.

key.description: <file>|<JSON pointer>. Use it as the key of the output.

file.description: The pack file the unit is in, the <file> of its key; one of the batch's files.

field.description: The name of the field the text is in, such as content.

speaker.description: Character id of the speaker. The speaker is named by the line's model, or by the speaker field of an RPG dialogue line; a name that is no known character is given as it is. "" when the line has none.

reason.description: Why the unit is pending: new, kr-changed, adjustment-expired, paratranz-repair, requeue or structural-fail.

prev_kr.description: The previous KR text, when the KR text changed.

prev_zh.description: The previous translation, when the KR text changed or a person sent the unit back (see hint).

draft.description: A draft to repair with as few changes as possible.

hint.description: Why a person sent the unit back for another translation (reason requeue): what to fix. Keep the rest of prev_zh as far as it can be kept.

en.description: The EN text aligned to the unit, with how it was matched. A help for understanding KR.

jp.description: The JP text aligned to the unit, with how it was matched. A help for understanding KR.

refs.description: Other translations (llc: simplified Chinese, ltm: traditional Chinese, same_text: the translations of the same KR sentence in other files, one line each as file (speaker): text) to look at. They are references, not answers.

keep.description: What the translation must keep from KR. Validation compares kinds and counts.

dante_wrapper.description: KR is a line of Dante wrapped in <...>; the translation must be wrapped too.

context.description: Story batches only: translated lines before, between and after the units. Read them for continuity; do not translate them.
